subject: One-time package swap & onboarding credit — approval request
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: One-time package swap request — CardioTech (deal CT-2028-0421)

Marissa,

Quick background: CardioTech (pilot-to-enterprise prospect) is ready to sign but procurement pushed back on the initial packaging. They need two immediate asks to get legal/PO moving: a one-time swap of 250k token burst (applied as a package swap rather than a recurring tier) and a $45k onboarding credit to offset integration costs. If we don't accommodate, we risk losing the renewal window and a larger multi-year commit later.

Summary impact (attached spreadsheet):
- Contract ACV (year 1): $480,000
- One-time onboarding credit: $45,000 (credit applied in first invoice)
- Package swap (non-recurring tokens): revenue-neutral across term but allows their procurement template to match our SKU mapping.
- Expected expansion probability next 18 months: >65% (sales judgment)

Asking for VP/CFO approval for a one-time onboarding credit + packaging exception (legal has redlines ready if we sign off). Legal flagged the package-swap language which needs exec signoff for non-standard SKU mapping.

Attachments: CTL-deal-summary-20280517.xlsx, proposed_amendment_one-time-package-swap.docx

Can you confirm if I should route this for Markus signoff or go straight to the CFO lane? We need a decision today to keep momentum.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-17T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: One-time package swap request — CardioTech (deal CT-2028-0421)

Thanks for the quick summary, Rishi.

I reviewed the spreadsheet — conservative P&L impact looks acceptable if we treat the onboarding credit as a marketing/promotional deduction and label the package swap explicitly as a non-recurring token allocation (no SKU reclassification). Two quick asks before I escalate:
1) Kimberly — do we have precedent for $45k onboarding credits in this segment? Need finance sign-off on treatment for revenue recognition and ARR windowing.
2) Markus — if finance signs, are you comfortable with exec-level exception for non-standard packaging? Legal redline attached shows the fallback language we propose.

If both answers are green, I'll draft the exception memo for VP/CFO signoff and copy legal. Rishi, please prepare a one-pager (customer value + expansion trigger) to attach to the memo.

-Marissa
Sr. Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: One-time package swap request — CardioTech (deal CT-2028-0421)

Marissa / Rishi,

Finance position: we have given onboarding credits in the past in the 10–12% range for strategic pilots; this request is ~9.4% of year 1 ACV, so within precedent for strategic logos. Treatment recommendations:
- Recognize credit as contra-revenue applied in month 1 invoice.
- No change to ARR baseline; credit reduces billed cash but not perpetual ARR calculation.
- Require clause that the onboarding credit is contingent on execution of the SOW and receipt of PO in 30 days.

I can greenlight subject to exec approval for packaging exception. Please capture the contingency language in the amendment.

Kimberly
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Legal <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Executive exception memo: CardioTech one-time package swap + onboarding credit (for signature)

Markus,

Per above thread, we are requesting your signoff (or CFO signoff) on a one-time exception for CardioTech:
- One-time onboarding credit: $45,000 (applied on first invoice, contingent on PO + SOW in 30 days).
- One-time package swap: convert 250k tokens into a non-recurring token package mapped to their procurement SKU (explicitly excluded from tiered usage calculations and future automatic renewal allocations).

Rationale: this is a near-term blocker to close an enterprise pilot that is highly strategic for our healthcare vertical; CardioTech controls a potential multi-region roll in H2 with >$1.8M ARR upside over 24 months if pilot metrics hold. Legal redline attached; finance has confirmed revenue treatment and contingency requirements.

Requested action: please reply with APPROVE or DECLINE. If APPROVE, indicate if you will sign or if you want the CFO to countersign. If you have edits to the amendment or need finance/legal to add specific fallback language, note below.

Attachments: CTL-deal-summary-20280517.xlsx, proposed_amendment_one-time-package-swap.docx, legal_redline_v1.pdf

Best,
Marissa
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive exception memo: CardioTech one-time package swap + onboarding credit (for signature)

Marissa / team — thanks for pulling this together. I reviewed the memo and attachments. I approve the one-time onboarding credit and package swap on the following conditions:
1) Customer signs the attached amendment with the contingency language Kimberly specified.
2) We add a 12-month no-refund clause for the swapped tokens (i.e., tokens are non-refundable and expire if unused after 12 months).
3) Rishi to secure an executive sponsor at CardioTech (VP Product or COO) on the SOW to improve expansion odds.

I will sign provided legal incorporates items (1) and (2). Please route the amendment to me after redlines. If legal signals any material risk, escalate to CFO.

-Markus
VP, Commercial Operations
